Checking the normalized titles against both saved review bodies confirms **8 inline + 23 unique body = 31 findings**, after removing sixteen repeated body occurrences. B2 and B11 remain separate ledger entries but share one underlying repair. Twenty-five findings receive bounded fixes or stronger independent oracles; six are explicitly rejected.

The accepted scope remains supported public behavior, including bugs already present on pinned master. `.fhir` is R5, `.fhirNext` is pinned R6 Snapshot 1, and the native clinical course remains private/unstable. Public producer/read-only formatter and saved public graph/wire workflows are supported. Authored values, independently authored endpoint units, source text and opaque metadata remain intact. No new clinical model, grammar vocabulary, native editor contract, generic malformed-input defense, unit conversion, downstream application repair or performance exclusion is added.

Root and three own ChatGPT workers used separate worktrees and ordinary repository execution; no validation host Codex/Gemini workers were launched. Supported public routes were compared against exact reviewed and frozen master artifacts before repairs. Focused tests and independent clinical oracles preceded integration. The mandatory integrated gates and independent raw-artifact audit below are complete; focused worker results are not substituted for final validation.

### Baseline distinctions and bounded implementation

Pinned master is `7d628239dc1cb5695c5fe1d8b9150682fe4d1adb`, with ESM digest `a1e143ee413b7a519ac5f99d591ef950cee92574f0b3995f366314181f96c0f2`. The exact reviewed ESM digest is `d2e0e77188e5fa79075650dcb632ddba25a0778cc8f4e1047f6aa5e832273dbf`.

Legacy site-reference recovery, the independent identified-slot edit, the annotated retired marker and the own-function resolver snapshot have demonstrated master/current regressions. Other accepted findings also fail on master or involve newer supported representations. Master treats the relative “until the next morning” end as opaque text plus a recurring morning event; it does not implement the current explicit unresolved boundary. In the same-day dated-eye case, master keeps the first dose but loses its successor, whereas the reviewed build lost the first dose. Master lacks corrected finite NEXT coordination and onset-only recurrence inheritance, and also has the two-day QAM short-preview defect. These differences are recorded rather than describing every finding as a clean regression.

For B2/B11, an initial noncyclic one-use fixture with one prior use was fully spent and correctly returned zero; it was rejected as defect evidence. The accepted public fixture uses an existing two-day cycle so its current phase quota is independent of the older rolling-cap record. One two-tablet administration becomes feasible after the calendar-month release, and the one-use quota proves two is optimal. The exact 20/60/1,455-minute horizons and fixed-elapsed/spent-quota controls isolate the defect. Partitioning the existing search by civil day keeps quota identity and the 32-slot/50,000-state budgets. Master returns zero because of an older cyclic quota issue. B3 and B4 likewise repair existing supported baseline defects, preserving actual quantities and units.

B12 uses frozen public saved graphs containing authored text and a quantity unit with no numeric value. The decoder already preserves that representation; only preview suppression lost the text. Numeric realization now controls whether the unit identity is hidden, with no invented value. Master already mishandles the companion and duplicates the partial theme unit. B17 extends only three existing typed locale codec fields. Both builds' configured lexical producer demonstrates that omission; the current semantic-proposal producer is additional evidence, not a capability attributed to master. The primitive count annotation case also preserves the distinction between metadata edits and the current numeric-count pause-retirement policy, which master does not implement in the same way.

I5 is explicitly not repaired. The observed current Nuuk sequence is March 21 23:30, March 29 00:30 at the cross-midnight gap, then April 5 23:30 instead of the logical April 4 date. Master also drifts to April 5 and retains 00:30. This remains the previously excluded logical-date stepping mechanism. Ordinary current New York timing returns from shifted March 8 03:30 to March 15/22 02:30; master retained 03:30 after the gap. No claim is made that all timezone cases are correct.

I7 is a separate rejection: its claimed first-dose loss does not occur through the exact public input. The boundary planner keeps both authored dose daughters; no malformed alternate source or private hand-built sign is used to force a fix. B13/B14 request the same unexported legacy clause-writer guarantee previously rejected. Actual public scalar/range controls retain exact foreign units and annotations through direct export and three cold saves on both builds. B10 and B22 request hypothetical future static-test or missing-build defenses. The agreed scope decisions are not reopened.

### Exact oracles and performance methodology

The original Dissolve cases now require the three-tablet amount on Dissolve itself, with the independent 100 mL vehicle and five-minute wait retained. Exact public edited-R6 English/Thai previews cover water/wait/drink and solvent variants. The source-only authored-directions fixture with independent administration caps requires the full edited two-tablet quantity/unit, rejecting 12 and 1.2; its shape is unchanged and it is not a unit-only source-quantity fixture. Both Thai meal-timed doses require the complete after-breakfast/lunch/dinner wording. The calendar-end fixture requires the complete one-tablet daily seven-day predecessor before its exact or implicit successor heading. The successor remains clockless.

Benchmark commit `c2d9111b0c246d22db332733fe34f0c5357fa8f4` strengthens two existing equivalence oracles without adding or removing scenarios. Prepared-drink equivalence requires the full unconditional two-tablet instruction and rejects an added pain condition, while allowing nonsemantic separators. The existing own-batch staged case requires all three stages in order, including their amounts, timing, durations and weekday set. Candidate failures remain case errors; a baseline with different clinical output retains raw timings without a regression verdict.

The available two-case oracle smoke used the frozen reviewed ESM and measured **zero timed comparisons**. The prepared-drink baseline remains an existing non-equivalent case because it omits the edited dose; both own-batch staged previews pass the new oracle. This smoke is not final-candidate performance validation. The final run must retain the established 184 paired scenarios, 117 public APIs, the same seven exclusions and each equivalent scenario's individual 4% ceiling. No cross-scenario averaging or new exemption may conceal a slower equivalent case.

The first integrated source gate at `1f45a7b8460ab63c0e56605c16bf5f9dbfef9e1c` reported **6,729 passed out of 6,730 assertions, with one failure**. It remains an unaccepted attempt. The independent public probe establishes the sole difference: the exact original annotated display is now retained in the existing inert source envelope at `step[0].component[0].extension`. Adding precisely that expected archive makes the full step array equal; all active clinical fields, top-level audit/signer annotations, normalized preview, cold-save result and original input remain exact. Root's test-only commit `7649c1056b0e5458bdc69db9d505260551287995` explicitly requires that exact archive and retains full step equality and all original assertions. Production source did not change: its digest remains `21436811d9c540f32864b21d0f236c7bc28d8d61c29cfb28048e44f0fb9ea80c`. ### Baseline distinctions and bounded implementation

I1 now uses the corrected, valid public fixture family described below. Its dose/delete/replace edits fail on the reviewed build and preserve the exact live modifier list on master and the current candidate, through three cold saves. The unchanged control works on all builds. The original malformed fixture producer is not used to claim a runtime defect.

I2 does not take master's three timestamps/five tablets as the intended oracle: two independent administrations on January 4 have different amounts and both count, so the supported fixture totals six tablets. I3 also is not a claim that master retained correct phase ownership; master promotes the anonymous limits in this family. Their independent current-interchange requirements justify the bounded existing-owner corrections.

I5's exact reviewed public selected result is already correct, although pinned master incorrectly emits an administered exact rate for the qualified form. I7 intentionally does not restore master's numeric two-day interpretation of “within two nights”: the complete advice and its authored period remain, with no 48-hour substitution. The per-night instruction policy is recorded in DIARY.md's earlier decision at line 12835 and reaffirmed by the typed-nightly/slash entry at line 14000.

I6's fractional-million family, I9's qualified daypart duplicate, and I10's compact R5 endpoint-unit error also occur on master. They are supported correctness repairs, not uniformly new regressions. I4 and I14 have separate public master controls: master recognizes the saline infusion and keeps the partial parallel members.

For I12, master keeps the medication name but omits 1 g; the reviewed build keeps 1 g but drops the medication name. For I13, master preserves 100 mL of water but still omits the administration dose. The corrections retain both independently authored facts, rather than treating either historical output as fully correct.

B4's literal “Mix with a household spoon” already renders correctly in English on the reviewed build. The ordinary saved no-article Object/Container forms “Mix with household spoon” and “Mix with bottle” demonstrate the lost With relation, and Thai also loses that relation. The bounded fallback preserves the saved relation; it does not add a new device vocabulary.

I11 acknowledges the real custom-code collision behavior difference from master while retaining the explicit owner rejection and existing surface precedence. The configured surface and a non-colliding custom code remain available. The owner's [scope correction](https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#issuecomment-7078410416) and [refactor-only directive](https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#issuecomment-7078752389), together with DIARY.md's surface-precedence/collision entries, remain the applicable scope evidence. I15 likewise acknowledges that master rereads a mutated nested batch export, while rejecting that workflow under README.md's immutable-output/import-boundary contract.

B1 accepts master's zero for the disjoint December window, not its incorrect behavior for other overlapping partial dates. B13 and B14 improve tests for behavior that already works on the reviewed build; neither is presented as a new runtime cadence/calendar repair.

### Findings and decisions

#### I1 — Keep the phase count when the same edit clears the legacy course count.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915019.

Preserve the independent phase count when an external R5 edit explicitly clears the saved legacy course count. The existing legacy migration now distinguishes an omitted modifier list from an explicit empty list; a new phase count of 2 or 3 remains active without reinterpreting it as the cleared course count. Master-produced unversioned 28-day rows give 14 or 21 uses respectively, while omitted and unrelated-modifier controls preserve legacy migration.

#### I2 — Check administration delay before restoring a dependent pause.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915035.

Restoration of a dependent saved pause now compares the predecessor's existing decoded administration offset, with omitted and zero offsets treated alike. A current 48-hour delay change retires the stale pause; unchanged timing, dose-only changes, annotations, and an equivalent zero offset preserve it. The external step's current start remains authoritative.

#### I3 — Do not restore a trailing draft in front of a newly appended step.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915047.

The trailing-draft receiver exception now applies only when no receiver exists in either saved or active steps. Appending a real step no longer inserts the old trailing draft ahead of it or changes its predecessor. The supported course-phase-event control executes January 2 and 3, rather than January 4 and 5. Pinned master does not understand that current boundary coding, so it is not a correctness oracle for this case.

#### I4 — Link implicit successors of a counted partial phase to its final predecessor.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915056.

The partial-parallel compiler now uses the existing phasePredecessors edges for an implicit successor after an exact finite phase, connecting every member of that immediately preceding phase in the same track. Execution carries the existing accepted completion point and exclusive fence through that edge. It does not borrow another eye's completion or invent an absolute origin. The original right-eye count-three case supplies 17 drops over five days with the independent left-eye BID track; reversing tracks gives the same result, the q12h control gives 9 over two days, and the coordinated predecessor control gives 23 over six days. Approximate durations remain unresolved. The existing exact pause chain keeps its original source and no-absolute-origin checks, with stronger actual-date oracles: five loading doses, two pause days, three days at two drops, then three drops; 41 drops over 12 days, November 30 total 4 and December 1 total 5. Reviewed code threw for these implicit successors; master also undercounted the initial cases, so its output was not adopted as the expected result. During integrated storage verification, the newly emitted predecessor identity exposed an existing codec combination of valueQuantity with child extensions. The real converter rejected it. The codec now uses its existing typed-start envelope when a newly generated dependency identity requires children, just as it already does for an end boundary. The complete corrected row survives actual converter and storage storage unchanged; clinical dates, quantities, and dependency identities are preserved. The failing output and the correction evidence remain archived. The first complete source run exposed an existing legacy-marker preservation oracle. Promotion is now limited to fresh syntax-generated markers; imported scalar markers retain their original active representation through three cold saves. The unchanged legacy test passes, and the complete new generated storage row remains exact. The failed full run is archived; no test or supplied fixture was weakened.

#### I5 — Keep an unchanged partial period limit when another maximum changes.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915069.

R5 representability of a period safety limit now requires the numeric numerator and denominator that the existing R5 safety codec actually consumes. An unchanged partial R6 limit therefore remains in the active preserved R6 data when another maximum changes. Unknown values and annotations remain supplied values; no numeric cap is invented. Fully valued edit/delete controls remain active, and the existing annotation-only raw R5 rule remains intact.

#### I6 — Report an unresolved explicit slot in supply totals when an exact event is also present.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915078.

The existing explicit-event reader now reports an unresolved supply slot when exact and month/year-precision events coexist and the actual quota is not filled. Exact candidate enumeration remains useful and unchanged. A private status handoff lets the existing scalar-count and ranged-cap admission owners decide completeness after their own quota accounting; the completion owner also retains an unknown horizon when partial events can still fill a slot. Count two with exact November 20 plus a December-only event is unresolved across November–December; count one, an already exhausted count, a disjoint partial month, and a final exact candidate filling the remaining slot retain known totals. The ranged and scalar-cap remaining-slot controls respectively return two and one tablets. Master fabricated month/year dates, which is not restored.

#### I7 — Keep fractional-week intervals on the elapsed grid when filtering weekdays.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915085.

Fractional weeks that do not normalize to whole civil days now use the existing elapsed-interval grid before weekday filtering. A 0.5-week interval is the same 84-hour grid as 3.5 days or 84 hours: from the January 1 origin, the Monday/Thursday filter admits January 8, 15, and 22 and no January 5 dose. Whole-week weekday positions stay unchanged. Authored period values and units remain untouched; master also had the incorrect next-due result.

#### I8 — Return zero before enumerating a fully spent ranged regimen.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915099.

The existing ranged schedule quota returns an empty known result immediately when history has exhausted it, before dates are enumerated. Count two with priorCount two, including the recorded-use control, yields zero; one remaining unresolved slot still raises the existing timing-required diagnostic. The scalar zero control remains unchanged.

#### I9 — Keep the supply timing diagnostic out of the phase completion probe.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915115.

Completion discovery now uses candidate semantics without propagating an actual-query supply diagnostic into its wider historical probe. The existing explicit-event reader still prevents a partial remaining event from falsely ending a stage at its last exact event. A November-only event gives zero for a disjoint December query and remains unresolved for an overlapping November query; exact-date and counted month/year controls retain their established behavior. No date is manufactured from month or year precision.

#### I10 — Preserve decimal time denominators when the amount and unit are attached.

Action: fix. Source: https://github.com/swittk/ezmedicationinput/pull/14#discussion_r4665915126.

The two existing attached rate-denominator unit patterns now accept ordinary decimal denominators such as /0.5h and /.5h, matching the already supported spaced spelling. Rate numerator, patient-mass denominator, time value, and time unit remain independent typed values. Spaced and /1h controls remain unchanged. The attached form was also lost by pinned master; this is an existing quantity-grammar correctness fix, not a new grammar family.

### Oracle changes, failed attempts and performance follow-up

All prior 6,952 source-test identities and multiplicities remain, with exactly 57 additions across the same 48 files. Identity retention does not imply every assertion stayed textually unchanged. For I13, root read the round-40 deferral and round-41 reopening before accepting the corrected existing bare-clock oracle; the same test identity, source and structural assertions remain, and independent controls preserve explicit daily repetition and same-day ordered clocks. Only that new oracle was corrected; the production change was unchanged. The final root focused run passed 1,196 cases. - Annotation-only end-boundary changes retain saved empty pauses and the current annotated end. Genuine completion changes still invalidate inappropriate restoration.
- Single-row previews use retained cycle offsets and the first nonempty administration without deleting retained empty draft stages.
- The current primary clinical condition governs its own threshold. Independent conditions and saved graph data remain intact.

### Timing, supply and instruction realization

- Clock windows respect calendar cadence; a two-day or weekly interval no longer opens on every date. Existing subday window behavior remains.
- Shifted supply counting uses the matching eligibility floor and preserves cadence origins and civil caps. Partial month/year events use their shifted possible-date envelope without inventing exact instants.
- Alternative selection retains authored empty timed stages in execution and preview. Shared-anchor inheritance compares exact and ranged offsets; a successor's own event window prevents predecessor-clock inheritance.
- Resolving the parser's typed “at the same time” reference no longer manufactures an empty advice array. This correction is confined to that producer branch; external FHIR fields and unrelated advice are preserved.
- A daypart can qualify its matching clock while other authored clocks remain. The compact and spaced AM/PM examples already preserved the approximate successor dose and now have exact controls.
- Qualified strength numerators do not produce unqualified ingredient estimates or concentration-based container conversions. Authored dose totals and independent volume estimates remain available. No invalid denominator-comparator handling was added.
- Explicit mixing Theme arguments take priority over nominal fallback. Dilution vehicles render once, and an independent Until result retains its relation alongside Before timing.
- Long Thai previews use the Buddhist date while preserving the authored time and offset. English/compact Thai behavior and exact wire instants remain covered.
- An empty dosage list returns an empty schedule without requiring a time zone.
